content.comment_body: Hello, I have a question. I have a Victron ESS system where I occasionally want to set the grid setpoint to -800W. Adjusting this value is possible using Modbus TCP, but I am unsure how to send a command to the Victron system. My goal is to set the grid setpoint to -800W when input 1 is activated on the [product_name]. Can anyone assist with this? Thank you in advance.
What should happen when input 1 switches to 0? Which value do you want transferred in that case? Should it be 0?

Without further details, I can only recommend checking the attachment. I'm unclear on several points: - Can the Modbus device operate as a server? - What are the IP addresses of the [product_name] and the Modbus device? - If the Modbus device is the server, what is its slave address? - What is the starting register number, 0 or 1?

Thank you for your time. I'll try to answer your questions: - Can the Modbus device act as a server? I don't think it's a Modbus server. - What are the IP addresses of the [product_name] and the Modbus device? [product_name]: 192.168.2.135 Victron: 192.168.2.152 - If the Modbus device is the server, what is its slave address? I don't know that. - What is the starting register number? For Victron, it's address + 1, so we need 2701.
Note: The [product_name] applies a +1 offset to addresses. If you want to write data from the [product_name] to the Modbus device, the [product_name] needs to be configured as the client.
One question: Which specific [product_name] model do you have? Please provide the complete [article_no].
You have not responded to my previous question...
When input 1 is deactivated, the setpoint should be 0 so no energy is fed back.
Alright, I'll create an example for you. Do you have an FS4 [product_name], or a [product_name] with [version_no]?
